name: Speaches
description: OpenAI API-compatible self-hosted speech server (formerly faster-whisper-server) that wraps faster-whisper (STT), Piper and Kokoro (TTS) behind a FastAPI/uvicorn HTTP service. Aims to be an 'Ollama for speech' with drop-in /v1/audio/transcriptions, /v1/audio/translations, /v1/audio/speech, and a realtime streaming API. No built-in authentication by default.
auth_notes: No authentication enforced by default. Speaches (and its faster-whisper-server predecessor) exposes the FastAPI app on 0.0.0.0:8000 with fully open /v1/* endpoints and interactive Swagger UI at /docs. Operators are expected to front the service with a reverse proxy for auth; most self-hosters and demo deployments do not. Because it is OpenAI-API-compatible, any exposed instance accepts Authorization: Bearer with any (or no) key value. App name, Swagger UI, and OpenAI-compat paths are rendered into served HTML, so instances are directly Shodan http.html-visible.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Direct project-name match in Swagger UI title/body or root JSON; high signal, low volume
Legacy project name still rendered in older Swagger info blocks and OpenAPI title; catches un-renamed deployments

Co-occurrence of the OpenAI STT transcription path AND the speech (TTS) path in the same Swagger doc is nearly unique to Speaches (combined STT+TTS server), separating it from transcription-only whisper wrappers
Version disclosure in Swagger UI info block or /openapi.json; use for CVE/version-targeted enumeration

known_vulns: No built-in auth — unauthenticated POST /v1/audio/transcriptions and /v1/audio/speech accept arbitrary audio/text from any source
Model management endpoints (POST/DELETE /v1/models/{id}) allow unauthenticated pull/download and deletion of models, enabling disk-fill DoS and arbitrary HuggingFace model fetch at operator cost
FastAPI /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json enabled by default — full API schema disclosure aids automated enumeration
Unrestricted file upload with no MIME/size validation in default config — multi-GB audio DoS exhausts GPU VRAM and host disk
No rate limiting — GPU compute-theft is trivially automated against transcription and TTS endpoints
Realtime streaming API (/v1/realtime WebSocket) exposed unauthenticated where enabled
HuggingFace Spaces demo deployments are publicly indexed with no auth and no usage controls
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Compute theft — open STT+TTS on GPU hosts is free inference at operator cost, automatable with any OpenAI SDK client pointed at the base URL. (2) Audio/text PII exfiltration — dictations, meeting audio, and synthesized-speech text prompts processed with no auth or audit logging. (3) Model-store abuse — unauthenticated model pull/delete enables disk exhaustion and forced download of attacker-chosen models. (4) Voice-clone data harvesting — combined audio+transcript and TTS synthesis on one host yields labeled voice datasets. (5) Realtime API abuse — where the streaming endpoint is on, an attacker gets a live low-latency speech pipe.
deployment_notes: Primarily Docker/Docker-Compose on CUDA GPU hosts (CPU mode too slow for production). Default bind 0.0.0.0:8000, uvicorn/FastAPI. Project renamed from faster-whisper-server to Speaches (speaches.ai); older deployments still self-identify by the legacy name in Swagger metadata. Common GPU-as-a-service hosts: Vast.ai, RunPod, Lambda Labs. HuggingFace Spaces demos frequent and publicly indexed. Directly Shodan http.html-visible via the served Swagger UI — no Censys/active-probe route needed for basic fingerprinting. Enterprise deployments front it with nginx/caddy + auth; hobbyist/research deployments frequently bind the raw 8000 port to the internet.
